title: Semantic Support Ticket Routing
business: Enterprise IT support teams managing high volumes of incoming technical tickets.
problem: Traditional keyword-based routing fails to capture the intent of complex technical queries, leading to misassigned tickets and increased resolution latency.
solution: The bge-base-en-v1.5 model transforms unstructured ticket descriptions into high-dimensional vectors, enabling semantic similarity matching against a knowledge base of resolved issue categories.
steps: Initialize the bge-base-en-v1.5 model using the HuggingFaceBgeEmbeddings interface.
Pre-process existing resolved support tickets into vector embeddings and store them in a vector database.
Convert incoming support tickets into vectors using the same model, optionally applying query instructions if the ticket is a short summary.
Perform a similarity search against the vector database to identify the most relevant historical resolution category.
Route the ticket to the support team associated with the highest-scoring historical category.
outcome: Improved accuracy in ticket classification and reduced manual triage time for support staff.
limitation: The model produces a similarity distribution typically in the range of [0.6, 1.0], meaning absolute scores are not directly interpretable as probability; developers must empirically determine a threshold based on their specific data distribution.

diagram.title: Semantic Ticket Routing Workflow
diagram.description: The process of converting raw text into actionable routing decisions via vector space.

code.content:
from langchain.embeddings import HuggingFaceBgeEmbeddings

# Initialize the model for Semantic Support Ticket Routing
model = HuggingFaceBgeEmbeddings(
    model_name="BAAI/bge-base-en-v1.5",
    encode_kwargs={'normalize_embeddings': True} # Normalize for cosine similarity
)

# Embed a new ticket
ticket_text = "System error 503 during database sync"
embedding = model.embed_query(ticket_text)
